subject: Future Tech
title: Metal 3D Printing
description: A quick, practical guide to Metal 3D Printing.

hook.text: Metal 3D printing fuses fine metal powder with lasers or electron beams to produce fully dense structural parts.

buildup.text: DMLS and SLM are the leading methods. A laser melts a 20-micron layer of titanium, steel, or aluminum powder per pass.

discovery.text: GE Aviation 3D-prints fuel nozzles for jet engines.

twist.text: That single nozzle is 25% lighter and five times more durable than the welded original.

climax.text: SpaceX prints SuperDraco rocket engine chambers. Boeing prints titanium brackets for the 787.

punchline.text: Metal parts once forged are now grown from powder.

quiz.question: How did GE improve its jet engine fuel nozzle with 3D printing?
